Figure 19 Silicone coated Mylar allows facile removal “peelability” of (A) AFL, (B) AFL on 1-layer ASL, and (C) AFL on 2-layer ASL (striations are due to slot-die gas adjustment for AFL coating from 1- layer to 2-layer ASL substrate). 3.5 Q5: In Q5, progress has been made to successfully demonstrate coating the ASL/AFL/GDC assembly as well as the 2-layer AFL/GDC. For the 3-layer ASL/AFL/GDC, both single-layer and double-layer ASL were coated. Approximately 10 ft or more for each of the conditions was fabricated with visual inspection of the resultant coating of good quality. During this quarter, the project has achieved the following:  Demonstrated coating of the 2 and three layers of: AFL/GDC, AFL/ASL and ASL/AFL/GDC via slot-die coating.  Fabricated varying thickness of ASL/ASL via slot-die coating from 100 - 700 µm.  Fabricated EEA with the minimal ASL thickness (~400 µm of the 2-layer ASL). The progress made in this period demonstrated the manufacturing potential when compared to the reverse order of coating which was reported in Q3. In the previous work, the thickest layer (ASL) was coated first and then subsequent coatings were deposited on this template. Variations in surface roughness caused the thin AFL layer (~18 µm) to have periodic areas of surface defects and also experienced some fluctuations in AFL layer thickness. This effect is mitigated by deposition of equivalent thickness of the ASL layer 13 onto the AFL and/or AFL/GDC as substrate. By reversing the order of coating, clear benefits have been observed in consistent layer thickness and removal of surface defects throughout the coating process. For future work requiring laminating the coated layers into a completed EEA, materials to be used have been fabricated, which includes 10 ft of ASL/AFL and > 5 ft of ASL/ASL/AFL along with > 20 ft of AFL/GDC, which will also be utilized in laminating multiple layers into an EEA. Additional material from the previously manufactured AFL/ASL and AFL/ASL/ASL coatings, reported during Q3, is also available for this purpose. The complete EEA was fabricated with > 5 ft of the 4-layer ASL/ASL/AFL/GDC including 2.5 ft with the targeted minimal ASL thickness and > 10 ft of 3-layer ASL/AFL/GDC showing excellent dry coating features such as exhibiting minimal surface defects and consistent layer thicknesses as well as excellent peeling from the Mylar substrate without falling off the Mylar during coating, drying and winding. Figure 20 shows (left) the 4-layer ASL/ASL/AFL/GDC coating wound up in the R2R slot-die coating process, coated within specifications for individual layer thicknesses as well as quality of final dry coatings, and (right) winding up > 5 ft of 4-layer ASL/ASL/AFL/GDC followed by > 10 ft of 3-layer ASL/AFL/GDC coating (spanning between the roller assembly). Additionally, the 2-layer ASL coatings were fabricated with uncalendered thicknesses ranging between 100 – 700 µm, with reproducible results of the minimum target thickness of 400 µm achieved in coating the ASL onto subsequent EEA layers.
